claims.text: Helm is a command-line package manager for Kubernetes that packages manifests as charts; a chart is a directory holding Chart.yaml, a values.yaml with default configuration values, and a templates/ directory of templates that, combined with values, produce valid manifest files.
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Introduction (Helm is the package manager for Kubernetes); Topics > Charts (The Chart File Structure)

claims.text: In Chart.yaml (apiVersion v2), name is the chart's name and version its SemVer version; appVersion is the version of the app it contains, informational only and need not be SemVer.
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Topics > Charts > The Chart.yaml File (version, appVersion)

claims.text: The web chart at stage-3 holds Chart.yaml, values.yaml, templates/deployment.yaml and templates/service.yaml; Chart.yaml sets name web, version 0.1.0, appVersion "2.10.0", and its comment says appVersion only says which Caddy the defaults run; neither template reads appVersion.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang deploy/helm/lessons/web/Chart.yaml lines 1-9 at stage-3; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/helm-template.txt lines 1-5

claims.text: Helm templates are text with {{ ... }} placeholders (Go template language), not parsed as YAML; {{ .Values.replicas }} reads the key replicas from the values, and {{ .Values.image.tag }} reads tag nested under image.
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Chart Template Guide > Getting Started; Values Files; Topics > Charts (Templates and Values)

claims.text: .Release.Name in a template is the release name given on the command line; for helm template it is the NAME argument, here web, so the rendered Deployment is named web and labelled app: web.
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Chart Template Guide > Built-in Objects (Release.Name); Helm Commands > helm template (usage NAME CHART); helm-template.txt

claims.text: Value precedence: the chart's values.yaml is the default, overridden by a user-supplied values file (-f), which is in turn overridden by --set parameters; a -f file overrides only the keys it sets.
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Chart Template Guide > Values Files (order of specificity); Using Helm > Customizing the Chart Before Installing

claims.text: values.yaml of the web chart sets replicas: 1, image.repository caddy and image.tag "2.10.0"; web-three-replicas.yaml sets only replicas: 3.
helm template renders chart templates locally and prints the output; it needs no kubeconfig, does not contact a cluster, and none of the server-side validity checks are done.
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Helm Commands > helm template (Synopsis: render chart templates locally; values looked up in-cluster are faked; no server-side testing)

claims.text: With KUBECONFIG pointing at a file that does not exist, helm template still renders the web chart with defaults, with -f and with --set.

Rendered results: defaults give replicas: 1 and image caddy:2.10.0; -f web-three-replicas.yaml gives replicas: 3 and caddy:2.10.0; adding --set replicas=5 --set image.tag=2.10.2 gives replicas: 5 and caddy:2.10.2.

--set key=value sets one value, with dots for nested keys (image.tag); with helm template it affects only that render and does not modify the chart's values.yaml, which still holds the defaults after both renders.
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Using Helm > The Format and Limitations of --set; helm-template.txt section 'values.yaml after both renders'

claims.text: helm template ... --set replicas=two prints replicas: two without error.
The Deployment API defines spec.replicas as an integer, so a string such as two is not a valid value.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io docs: Reference > Kubernetes API > Workload Resources > Deployment (DeploymentSpec.replicas: int32)

claims.text: The web template is the Deployment of deploy/k8s/lessons/web-deployment.yaml with placeholders for name, replicas and image; the image is built as "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}".

A chart contains no container image: the manifest names the image, and when the Pod starts, the kubelet pulls it from a registry if the node does not already have it (IfNotPresent for a non-latest tag).
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Topics > Charts (chart = collection of files); kubernetes.io docs: Concepts > Containers > Images

claims.text: helm template NAME CHART takes the name first, then the chart path; -f passes a values file; --show-only <path> limits the output to the manifest rendered from that template (here the Deployment, not the Service).
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Helm Commands > helm template (usage, flags -f/--values, -s/--show-only)

claims.text: In the Try it render, the Deployment shows replicas: 1 and image: "caddy:2.10.2", and git status --short deploy/helm prints nothing.
claims.source_hint: follows from claims 6, 10, 11 and helm-template.txt; run locally to confirm

claims.text: In the Đơn Hàng lab, helm runs on the host (Helm 3.19 is a listed host tool for scripts/k8s/), so the Try it needs no cluster.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang STAGE.md at stage-3 (host tools: Helm 3.19); helm-template.sh line 3
